capabilities: cite copied PDF selections as author-date, APA, Harvard, or numbered citation labels
import annotations from Zotero, Kindle, Apple Books, and Apple Preview into Markdown notes
generate and refresh a managed reference list for the current note
view and annotate DOCX, Google Docs, and text files with Markdown annotation threads
fill empty reading-note properties from Zotero and PDF metadata
disambiguation: Not a replacement for Zotero; Zotero still provides citation metadata and formatted references while this plugin handles the Obsidian PDF link, highlight, paste, and note-writing workflow.
extras: Direct PDF-editing commands can modify PDF files in the vault, so the README advises keeping backups; some styling features require the Style Settings plugin; installable via BRAT; column-aware reading mode is described as experimental; handwriting from Nebo or OneNote is not transcribed or OCR'd.
intentEvidence: It is a fork of PDF++, with extra tools for quieter scholarly notes
motivation: Part of the author's larger Scholia direction: helping a research library become easier to cite, review, and turn into finished scholarly notes.
problem: Obsidian's PDF workflow exposes technical link labels (file names, page indexes, colors) and lacks citation formatting, reference-list generation, and import of annotations from reading apps for scholarly writing.

relations.evidence: PDF Scholia Scribe is a maintained fork of PDF++
the plugin may query the Zotero local API at the configured base URL

summary: Fork of PDF++ that adds citation-style PDF link labels, Zotero and reading-app annotation import, DOCX viewing, and portable annotation threads.
